target:
inductive Form : Type
  | atom (r x y : ℕ) : Form
  | fls : Form
  | imp (φ ψ : Form) : Form
  | all (x : ℕ) (φ : Form) : Form
  | K (φ : Form) : Form

def neg (φ : Form) : Form := imp φ fls

def and (φ ψ : Form) : Form := neg (imp φ (neg ψ))

def iff (φ ψ : Form) : Form := and (imp φ ψ) (imp ψ φ)

def ex (x : ℕ) (φ : Form) : Form := neg (all x (neg φ))

def Def6 (x : ℕ) : Form → Prop
  | atom _ a b => x = a ∨ x = b
  | fls => False
  | imp φ ψ => Def6 x φ ∨ Def6 x ψ
  | all y φ => x ≠ y ∧ Def6 x φ
  | K φ => Def6 x φ

def Def7 (x y : ℕ) : Form → Form
  | atom r a b => atom r (if a = x then y else a) (if b = x then y else b)
  | fls => fls
  | imp φ ψ => imp (Def7 x y φ) (Def7 x y ψ)
  | all z φ => if z = x then all z φ else all z (Def7 x y φ)
  | K φ => K (Def7 x y φ)

def Def8 (y x : ℕ) : Form → Prop
  | atom _ _ _ => True
  | fls => True
  | imp φ ψ => Def8 y x φ ∧ Def8 y x ψ
  | all z φ => z = x ∨ ¬ Def6 x φ ∨ (z ≠ y ∧ Def8 y x φ)
  | K φ => Def8 y x φ

divergences.description: Relative to Reinhardt's passages (which use the language of arithmetic with constants, function symbols, equality, and term substitution p(x/t)), the Lean formalization omits arithmetic symbols, terms, and equality and instead uses countably many binary relation symbols (atom r x y), restricting substitution (Def7) and substitutability (Def8) to variables only; this restriction is explicitly acknowledged by the author as declared separately.

judgement.summary: The Lean definitions faithfully formalize Reinhardt's modal formation rule (adding K for B), standard classical derived connectives, and the three standard syntactic notions—free occurrence (Def6), substitution of free occurrences (Def7), and substitutability (Def8)—with substitution properly passing inside K. The only divergence from the source passages is the already-declared restriction from the language of arithmetic (with equality and term substitution) to a purely binary-relational language with variable-for-variable substitution.
